evals.prompt: I want a game like Crossy Road where we hop across a busy road on our phones. We'll all be at my house on the same Wi-Fi. First one across wins.
evals.expected_output: The first grill round asks in one message whether anyone will play on a phone and how they should move, offering swipe (one hop or step) versus a little stick (keep moving), together with the other game questions. The skill does not scaffold or write game.js until they confirm a four-or-five-sentence replay. They named Crossy Road, so one Research brief may say what to borrow and what not to copy. After confirm, the project is scaffolded with --shape=hop, which sets --render=3d, and --transport=local. The main model then edits that hop game.js. It does not launch Look and Flow, and it does not invent a new architecture. game.js sets input.touch to 'swipe', keeps lane and rowAt, keeps keyboard working, and does not raise TICK_HZ or edit core/.
